approach: Point OLY-B-O1-01 in docs/spec.toml at the existing `athena_gate::invariant::bootstrap_range` (rule M6) with a one-line measure ending `status: not shown` that names the test. Add the integration test crates/athena-gate/tests/bootstrap_requirement.rs. It holds a pure `check_entry(&str) -> Result<(), String>` that validates a spec entry. One test feeds it a literal copy of the base entry (mechanism "none") and expects Err, so the failure without the change is shown in the same run. Another feeds it the real docs/spec.toml entry and expects Ok. A third test builds a throwaway repo and calls the real `bootstrap_range` for Open and then ClosedThrough. Also register the new test unit in xtask/shard-timings.txt (needed by `checked_in_timings_cover_every_workspace_test_unit`), add a CHANGELOG bullet, and add one doc-comment line on `bootstrap_range`. No gate behavior changes and Cargo.toml stays unchanged.

decisions.choice: Mechanism is the existing `athena_gate::invariant::bootstrap_range` (rule M6). The measure says 'v0 stays small' is not mechanically enforced and ends `status: not shown`.
decisions.reason: invariant.rs:60-79 defines the range and invariant.rs:175-197 refuses `Athena-Job: bootstrap` after it closes, which mechanises 'recorded as such, the only work outside Athena'. The user accepted this reading. xtask/tests/spec.rs requires only that the measure ends `status: <label>`. The measure must contain `status:` once and stay on one line.

rejected.option: Add a size limit for v0
rejected.why: Out of scope; there is no defined threshold.

rejected.option: Add an `athena status` label such as `status: bootstrap`
rejected.why: Out of scope; it would change STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS. `athena status` already prints a `bootstrap` line from bootstrap_view (status.rs:1184), but the plan adds no label.

decisions.choice: The spec-entry check is a pure function `check_entry(&str)`. The test runs it on a literal copy of the base entry (expects Err) and on the real file's entry (expects Ok).
decisions.reason: This answers finding 3. The test then fails on the base text inside one `cargo test` run, with no need to restore the base docs/spec.toml in a scratch copy. The base-entry literal is a fixed fixture; the logic under test is the production spec file plus the checker, not a double.

rejected.option: Only assert against the real file and argue the base failure by reading
rejected.why: Nothing would be run against the base tree.

rejected.option: Ask the verifier to restore the base spec in a scratch copy
rejected.why: The verifier's command list has no copy or checkout command.

decisions.choice: Keep the Open/ClosedThrough range test but do not count it as evidence that a test fails without the change.
decisions.reason: This answers finding 4. It calls the unchanged `bootstrap_range`, so it passes on the base tree. It only gives the `bootstrap` filter a direct range check. Criterion 2 rests on the spec-entry tests. Criterion 3 rests on the existing M6 test, which drives `check` (invariant.rs:1102-1122).

rejected.why: The brief lists a gate test file. It is cheap, and it adds a direct check that the outcome record closes the range.

rejected.option: Add a testkit dev-dependency to run the full `check` from the integration test
rejected.why: The in-source test already covers it; this would force a Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock change.

decisions.choice: Add `athena-gate --test bootstrap_requirement 5.00` to xtask/shard-timings.txt after line 59 (`athena-gate --lib 10.00`). Label it an estimate in the changelog bullet.
decisions.reason: This answers finding 1. xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs:410-421 requires the timed units to equal the workspace's test units. A new tests/*.rs file adds a unit. The sorted position is after `--lib` because `--test` sorts after `--doc` and `--lib` (xtask/shard-timings.txt:58-59). The 5.00 follows the precedent of `athena-core --test model_roster 5.00` (line 53).

rejected.option: Run `cargo run -p xtask -- shard-timings` to measure the seconds
rejected.why: It reruns every unit and rewrites the whole file; a one-line estimate is enough and matches earlier changelog entries (CHANGELOG.md:867).

steps: Edit docs/spec.toml at OLY-B-O1-01 (line 2163). Replace the mechanism line with text naming `athena_gate::invariant::bootstrap_range` (rule M6: `Athena-Job: bootstrap` commits are accepted only until records/jobs/bootstrap/outcome.json closes the range). Keep owner = "Athena". Write a single-line measure naming `cargo test -p athena-gate bootstrap` and crates/athena-gate/tests/bootstrap_requirement.rs, stating that 'v0 stays small' is not mechanically enforced, and ending `status: not shown`. Use `status:` only once. Leave the statement and source lines alone.

Create crates/athena-gate/tests/bootstrap_requirement.rs. Add `repo_file` as in model_roster.rs:11-16. Add `check_entry(text: &str) -> Result<(), String>`. It slices from `id = "OLY-B-O1-01"` to the next `[[requirement]]`, then rejects `mechanism = "none"`, a missing `athena_gate::invariant::bootstrap_range`, a missing `owner = "Athena"`, and a `measure = ` line that does not end `status: not shown` or does not name `bootstrap`. Test `spec_entry_names_the_bootstrap_range_gate` runs it on the real docs/spec.toml. Test `base_entry_is_rejected` runs it on a literal copy of the base entry (mechanism none, measure 'The spec gap list; status: requirement') and asserts Err. Test `bootstrap_range_is_open_then_closed_by_the_outcome_record` makes a tempdir, runs `Git::isolated`, `git init -q -b main`, writes a file and commits it, and asserts `bootstrap_range(&git, "HEAD")` is `BootstrapRange::Open`. It then writes records/jobs/bootstrap/outcome.json (JSON from invariant.rs:1109 with `through_commit` set to the first commit id), commits it, and asserts `ClosedThrough(<id>)`.
Add one doc-comment line on `bootstrap_range` in crates/athena-gate/src/invariant.rs (line 67) naming OLY-B-O1-01. Make no other code change.
Add `athena-gate --test bootstrap_requirement 5.00` to xtask/shard-timings.txt directly after `athena-gate --lib 10.00` (line 59), keeping the sorted order.

Add a first bullet under [Unreleased] / Added in CHANGELOG.md, in the style of the OLY-B-SET-02 entry (CHANGELOG.md:26-32). It says: OLY-B-O1-01 now has a mechanism, `bootstrap_range` (rule M6); the measure is `status: not shown` and names the tests; 'v0 stays small' stays prose; the gate and the records are unchanged; the new test file is registered in xtask/shard-timings.txt with a 5.00 s estimate.

Run `cargo fmt --all`. Then run `cargo test -p athena-gate`, `cargo test -p xtask --test ci_shards`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`, to cover the xtask spec test, the shard-timings check and the boundary scan over the new text.

risks.risk: The xtask measure parse uses `rsplit_once("status:")` (spec.rs:194-213). A second `status:` or a multi-line measure would break the ending.
risks.mitigation: Keep the measure on one line with `status:` only once, at the end. `check_entry` applies the same rule to the real entry.

risks.risk: The literal base-entry fixture in `base_entry_is_rejected` could drift from the real spec.
risks.mitigation: It is a fixed copy of the base entry, kept only to show that the checker rejects `mechanism = "none"`. It does not read docs/spec.toml, so later spec edits cannot break it.

risks.risk: The temp-repo test needs a git binary and identity settings in the checks' environment.
risks.mitigation: `Git::isolated` sets author, committer and gpgsign=false, the same setup as the in-source helpers (gate/src/lib.rs:396-418). The test runs `git init -q -b main` itself.

risks.risk: The outcome JSON in the range test drifts from the `athena.outcome/1` schema, so parsing fails and `ClosedThrough` carries an empty id.
risks.mitigation: Copy the JSON from the string at invariant.rs:1109, which the existing test already parses, and assert `ClosedThrough(id)` with the real commit id.

risks.risk: The 5.00 s timing in shard-timings.txt is an estimate and could skew shard balance slightly.
risks.mitigation: The changelog bullet labels it an estimate. Balance does not affect correctness, and the file is refreshable with `cargo run -p xtask -- shard-timings`.

risks.risk: 'v0 stays small' is not enforced, so the requirement is only partly mechanised.
risks.mitigation: The measure says so and ends `status: not shown`. The changelog bullet repeats it.

demonstrations.method: The test `spec_entry_names_the_bootstrap_range_gate` reads the real docs/spec.toml, slices the entry at `id = "OLY-B-O1-01"` up to the next `[[requirement]]`, and runs `check_entry` on it. Then `git diff docs/spec.toml` shows the edited lines.
demonstrations.observes: The real entry has no `mechanism = "none"` and its mechanism text contains `athena_gate::invariant::bootstrap_range`. It keeps `owner = "Athena"`. Its single-line measure names `cargo test -p athena-gate bootstrap` and ends with `status: not shown`.
demonstrations.fails_without: On the base tree the entry has `mechanism = "none"` (docs/spec.toml:2164) and measure 'The spec gap list; status: requirement', so `check_entry` returns Err and the test fails.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point: the pure `check_entry(&str)` in the new test file, applied to the repository's real docs/spec.toml read via `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")/../..` (the model_roster.rs:11-16 approach). No double. Added by plan step 2; the spec file exists.

demonstrations.method: The same run holds `base_entry_is_rejected`. It calls `check_entry` on a literal copy of the base entry (lines 2163-2169 of the base docs/spec.toml, with `mechanism = "none"` and measure 'The spec gap list; status: requirement') and asserts Err naming the mechanism. `spec_entry_names_the_bootstrap_range_gate` asserts the real entry is Ok. `bootstrap_range_is_open_then_closed_by_the_outcome_record` also runs.
demonstrations.observes: All three tests pass with the change. Because `base_entry_is_rejected` passes, the checker provably rejects the base entry, so the real-file test would fail on the base tree. The test file does not exist at base, so the run itself fails there with 'no test target'.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the base docs/spec.toml, `spec_entry_names_the_bootstrap_range_gate` fails on `mechanism = "none"`. If the checker accepted the base entry, `base_entry_is_rejected` would fail.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point: `check_entry` in the new test file, with the fixture being a literal base-entry string compiled into the test. The checker is real production-spec logic and is not replaced by the fixture. The range test calls the real `athena_gate::invariant::bootstrap_range(&Git, "HEAD")` (invariant.rs:68) on a `tempfile::tempdir` repo made with `athena_git::Git::isolated` (Cargo.toml:11-19 already lists both as dependencies). Precondition: a git binary and one commit. Added by plan step 2; `bootstrap_range` and `Git::isolated` exist.

demonstrations.method: The `bootstrap` filter runs the existing in-source `bootstrap_commits_pass_while_the_range_is_open_and_not_after` (invariant.rs:1102-1122) and the new `bootstrap_range_is_open_then_closed_by_the_outcome_record`. The existing test builds an owner repo, commits `Athena-Job: bootstrap` while the range is open, adds records/jobs/bootstrap/outcome.json, then adds a late bootstrap commit and judges it.
demonstrations.observes: Bootstrap commits pass while the range is open and at the closing commit. A late `Athena-Job: bootstrap` commit after `through_commit` gets exactly one violation (assert at invariant.rs:1121). The new test sees `Open` then `ClosedThrough(<commit id>)`.
demonstrations.fails_without: If rule M6 accepted bootstrap commits after the outcome record (the `ClosedThrough` arm, invariant.rs:181-196), the `assert_eq!(judge(&git, "HEAD").len(), 1)` at invariant.rs:1121 fails. If `bootstrap_range` ignored the outcome file, the new range test fails. This existing gate test is the evidence for criterion 3. The new range test adds only a direct check.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points: `invariant::check` (invariant.rs:102) via the in-source `judge` helper (invariant.rs:885) and `owner_repo()` (invariant.rs:892), plus `bootstrap_range`. Fixtures are real temporary git repos made inside the tests. All exist today (read); no new seam is needed beyond the new range test (step 2).

demonstrations.method: The verifier runs each check as its own command: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`.
demonstrations.observes: No fmt diff and no clippy warnings. Every test passes, including xtask `every_active_requirement_has_a_mechanism_an_owner_and_a_measure` (spec.rs:627, which uses `check_how_it_is_met`, spec.rs:194), xtask `checked_in_timings_cover_every_workspace_test_unit` (ci_shards.rs:411) and the policy scans.
demonstrations.fails_without: A measure without a trailing `status: <label>` fails the xtask spec test. A missing shard-timings line fails ci_shards.rs:411, which is why step 4 adds it.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points: the workspace cargo commands, the xtask spec parse and the shard oracle in xtask/tests. All exist today (read).
